summary: Client-subnet preservation through VPCE NAT rotates source IPs causing OCSP rate-limits and intermittent gRPC auth failures
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (DataSentry) reports intermittent authentication failures when calling Redwood control plane from their Private deployment (VPCE). Failures correlate with OCSP responder 429s and the control-plane returning transient 401/403s to serving nodes which then surface as gRPC auth errors to the SDK.

Impact:
- Serving nodes intermittently fail requests requiring token refresh; customer sees 401/403 followed by backoff and higher latency for ~5-15s bursts.
- Affects production traffic in us-east-1; roughly 2-3% of requests during peak egress churn windows.

Environment:
- Private deployment using VPCE with customer-managed NAT gateway cluster (autoscaling NAT instances behind TGW).
- VPCE configured with client-subnet preservation enabled on the egress path to allow downstream ACLs.
- Control plane expects relatively stable source IPs for OCSP and auth caching.

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Customer runs sustained batch requests from serving pool (nightly heavy traffic).
2) NAT pool churn / client-subnet-preservation leads to frequent source IP rotation for outbound connections to OCSP and token endpoints.
3) OCSP responder rate-limits or returns 429 to multiple distinct ephemeral source IPs from same customer.
4) Control-plane fails to validate certificates or marks cached cert validations stale -> returns transient 401/403 to serving nodes.

Observed logs and telemetry:
- Control-plane logs show clusters of OCSP 429s at 2026-03-10T23:14:xxZ and 23:27:xxZ.
- Serving node logs show immediate token refresh attempts, then gRPC auth failures: "rpc error: code = Unauthenticated desc = token validation failed".
- VPC flow logs show outbound connections to ocsp.example-ca.com from numerous ephemeral source IPs within a short timeframe.
- Customer attached tcpdump (pcap) showing NAT source port reuse and change of source IP across series of OCSP requests.

Notes on impact threshold and priority justification:
Because auth failures cause user-visible 401s and increased error rates during nightly batches and the customer is on a Private plan, this is prioritized as P1 / Sev1 for investigation and temporary mitigation recommendations.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Luis Ramirez (Customer): Initial report attached with pcap and control-plane request IDs. Customer says issue spikes during scheduled nightly shard fetches.
2026-03-10 11:03 - Support (Maya Chen): Acknowledged. Collected request IDs and escalated to Networking SRE. Requested sample flow logs and NAT instance autoscale events.

2026-03-10 14:45 - Networking SRE (Arjun Patel): Observed OCSP 429 clusters and rapid source IP churn from VPCE egress. Hypothesis: client-subnet preservation combined with autoscaling NAT results in many distinct public IPs mapped to same private prefix, triggering OCSP throttling per-IP.
2026-03-10 16:02 - Customer (DataSentry - Ops): Confirmed NAT autoscale happened at 23:10 UTC and 23:25 UTC aligned with failures. They use TGW + autoscaling NAT instances with no static EIP pool.

2026-03-11 09:10 - Support (Maya Chen): Provided immediate mitigation steps (below). Opened PR to control-plane to add softer retry for OCSP 429 so auth flapping doesn't immediately surface as 401 to serving nodes.

2026-03-12 12:30 - Engineering (K. Nguyen): Deployed an auth-sidebackoff change to treat OCSP 429 as transient and extend token cache TTL by 15s in control-plane canary; monitoring for reduction in 401 spikes.

2026-03-13 07:22 - Customer (DataSentry - Ops): Applied recommended NAT static-EIP pool and confirmed significant reduction in source-IP churn during nightly load. Reporting near-zero auth errors in latest runs.
2026-03-13 11:00 - Support (Maya Chen): Marking as In Progress while monitoring. Requested follow-up in 72 hours to close if no recurrence.
investigation_notes: Validated correlation between NAT autoscaling events and OCSP 429 clusters using flow logs and control-plane telemetry.
OCSP responder applies per-source-IP rate limits; rotating source IPs from same private prefix defeats downstream caching assumptions.
Control-plane currently treats OCSP 429 as a hard failure which triggers immediate token validation failure for active sessions.
Reproduced locally by simulating multiple ephemeral public IPs issuing OCSP checks against staging responder and observed 429s and then token invalidation events.

Checked related tickets SUP-712345 and SUP-712987 for similar NAT/TGW interactions; this one differs because client-subnet preservation intentionally preserves private-client-subnet but NAT still rotates public EIP per instance.
resolution:
Temporary mitigation provided to customer: (1) Configure a small static EIP pool for NAT instances to preserve stable outbound public IPs during autoscale, (2) If using TGW+autoscale, enable sticky EIP assignment to NAT instances. On Redwood side: deployed control-plane change to treat OCSP 429s as transient (soft backoff) and extend token cache TTL by 15s in canary to reduce auth flapping.

Follow-up actions and owners:
- Customer: keep static EIP pool and monitor for 72 hours (DataSentry Ops).
- Networking SRE: monitor OCSP 429 rate and auth 401 counts for affected control-plane shard (Arjun Patel).
- Auth/Control-plane: roll out soft-backoff change to all regions after 48h canary period (K. Nguyen).

Status: Mitigation applied and verified by customer on 2026-03-13; monitoring ongoing. Recommend closure if error rates remain below baseline for 72 hours.
